title: The Wizard of the Emerald City
author: Alexander Volkov
short_summary: A girl named Ellie, her house and her little dog Totoshka are carried off by a hurricane into the Magic Land, where the falling house crushes the wicked witch Gingema. The good witch Villina reads in her book that to get back to Kansas, Ellie must first help three beings have their dearest wishes granted. Along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City she gathers the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman and the Cowardly Lion — and ahead of them wait an ogre, a poppy field, Bastinda, and Goodwin the Great and Terrible.
extended_summary:
The wicked witch Gingema conjures a hurricane to destroy the world, but the good witch Villina turns it so that Ellie's house falls directly on Gingema. Ellie lands in the Magic Land, where her dog Totoshka suddenly begins to speak. Villina looks in her magic book and explains: the great Goodwin of the Emerald City can send Ellie home, but only if she first helps three beings have their dearest wishes granted.

Along the yellow brick road Ellie lifts the Scarecrow off his pole (he wants brains), oils the rusted Tin Woodman (he wants a heart), and takes along the Cowardly Lion (he wants courage). An ogre carries Ellie off and her friends rescue her; in the poppy field they are saved by Ramina, queen of the field mice, who gives Ellie a little silver whistle. At the gates, the guardian Faramant hands out green spectacles and the long-bearded soldier Din Gior lets them in to Goodwin, who appears to each of them in a different shape.

Goodwin agrees to help if they defeat the wicked Bastinda. Captured in her country, Ellie learns that Bastinda is terrified of water and throws a bucket over her; the witch melts. The friends return with the golden cap that commands the Flying Monkeys. Goodwin turns out to be an ordinary man from Kansas who arrived long ago in a balloon; he gives the Scarecrow, the Woodman and the Lion the things they believe in, and flies home, leaving the Scarecrow to rule. Ellie herself is sent back to Kansas by the good witch Stella, who tells her the secret of the silver shoes.

questions.prompt: What happens to the little dog Totoshka as soon as he arrives in the Magic Land?

options: He begins to speak in a human voice
He grows to the size of a large dog
He stops being frightened of anything
He finds the way back to Kansas

questions.explanation: Every animal talks in the Magic Land, and Totoshka is no exception — it is he who later exposes Goodwin by looking behind the screen. This is one of the ways Volkov's book differs from the American original: the dog is a character in his own right, not a pet.

questions.prompt: What does Villina read in her magic book — the condition Ellie must meet before she can go home?

options: She must help three dearest wishes come true
She must find Gingema's three magic objects
She must live in the Magic Land for one year
She must defeat both of the wicked witches

questions.explanation: This condition is the engine of the whole book: Ellie cannot simply walk to Goodwin and ask. Getting home is tied directly to whether she helps three strangers get the thing each of them lacks.

questions.prompt: Who sends the hurricane — and what happens to her in the end?

options: Gingema; Ellie's house falls on her
Bastinda; the same hurricane carries her off
Villina; she later regrets doing it
Stella; she wanted to invite Ellie over

questions.explanation: Gingema conjured the hurricane, and Villina steered it so that the house came down on top of her. The wicked witch is killed by her own magic — and all that is left of her is the pair of silver shoes that will eventually carry Ellie home.

questions.prompt: Ramina, queen of the field mice, gives Ellie a little silver ___ to call for help when she needs it.
questions.explanation: The present looks like nothing and turns out to be a rescue. Volkov likes objects of this kind: the most useful things in the book are not a magic wand but a bucket of water, a silver whistle, and knowing when to ask for help.

questions.prompt: Put the events of Ellie's journey in the order they happen.

items: The house lands and crushes the wicked Gingema
Ellie lifts the Scarecrow down off his pole
The friends oil the rusted Tin Woodman
The Cowardly Lion joins the company
The travellers enter the Emerald City
Bastinda melts under a bucket of water

questions.explanation: The companions join strictly in turn, and that is deliberate: first the one who needs a mind, then the one who needs a heart, and only then the one who needs courage. Volkov lines them up in the order the journey will require them.

questions.prompt: Match each character to what they do in the book.

right: The gatekeeper who hands out green spectacles
The long-bearded soldier who admits visitors
The queen of the field mice, who gives a whistle
The mistress of the Purple Country and the Monkeys

questions.explanation: These are four characters the American version does not have in this form: Volkov gave the Emerald City its own inhabitants, with names and personalities. Faramant and Din Gior go on to appear in the later books of the series.

questions.prompt: Some of the wonders in this book are real magic and some are pure trickery. Sort them.

content.groupB: A trick or an ordinary dodge

options.label: Silver shoes that carry you anywhere at all
A golden cap that commands the Flying Monkeys
The talking animals of the Magic Land
Green spectacles that make everything look green
A huge talking head in the throne room
Bran and needles handed over as brains

questions.explanation: Half the marvels in this book are stage props. The interesting part is that the trickery works: the Scarecrow with bran in his head really does start thinking clearly, because now he believes in himself. Volkov does not sneer at this — he shows you how it operates.

questions.prompt: Goodwin appears to each visitor in a different shape — a head, a beast, a ball of fire. Why?

options: He is an ordinary man keeping up his reputation
He cannot hold any one shape for very long
The law of the Emerald City requires it of him
He is testing whether visitors will recognise him

questions.explanation: Goodwin is a man from Kansas who drifted here in a balloon, and he can do no magic whatsoever. Screens, ropes and green glass are his entire toolkit, and his power depends completely on nobody looking behind the curtain. Until Totoshka does.

questions.prompt: Goodwin gives the Scarecrow bran and needles instead of brains, the Woodman a cloth heart, and the Lion a drink 'for courage'. It is a fraud — and yet all three behave more confidently afterwards. Did he actually help them? Give your reasons.
questions.explanation: Both positions can earn full marks. A strong 'he helped' answer notices that the confidence is genuine and that each of the three had already shown intelligence, kindness and courage in action. A strong 'he cheated them' answer notices that he posed as a wizard for years, demanded Bastinda's death as his price, and nearly got the friends killed. Accept either, with a reason from the book.

questions.prompt: Goodwin never gave anyone real magic — he gave them an object that made them believe in themselves. If you came to him with a wish of your own, what would you ask for, and what 'fake' thing could he hand you that would still work?
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer. A strong answer names the wish, names a specific object, and explains why the object would work — in other words, it repeats Goodwin's own trick. An answer that asks for genuine magic has missed the point of the question.

questions.prompt: The terrifying Bastinda had one weakness: more than anything in the world she was afraid of ___.
questions.explanation: She had not washed for years rather than risk it. Ellie throws the bucket in a temper, without even knowing what she is doing — and the most feared witch of the Purple Country simply melts away.

questions.prompt: Goodwin's balloon leaves without Ellie. So how does she finally get back to Kansas?

options: The silver shoes carry her when she commands them
The Flying Monkeys carry her across the desert
Ramina's mice dig a tunnel underneath the desert
The Scarecrow builds her another balloon

questions.explanation: It is the good witch Stella who reveals the shoes' secret: they could have taken Ellie anywhere all along. The means of escape was on her feet from the first day — but only after she had walked the whole road and met Villina's condition.
